intro: Drake Maye's fractured fibula and Justin Herbert's concussion shook the AFC on the same weekend the Colts cut Daniel Jones. The Bills defense keeps the end zone closed, and Thanksgiving week opens with the NFC North lead on the line in Detroit. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Drake Maye fractures fibula as Patriots reach bye at 5-5
top.dek: Tests showed a fractured right fibula for the Patriots quarterback, who got hurt on the first drive of the loss to Detroit in Munich. No surgery is needed, but Mike Vrabel does not expect him back for the Nov. 29 game at the Chargers, and the rest of the season is in question.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers fall to 1-9
top.dek: Herbert took six sacks in the 27-24 loss to the Jets, two on the final possession, and the team announced the protocol after the game. His status for Week 12 is open, and rookie edge rusher Akheem Mesidor also left with an ankle injury.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Dak Prescott throws four touchdowns without a pick in Cowboys rout
top.dek: Prescott went 28 of 33 for 325 yards in the 51-30 win over Tennessee and ran in another score. He has 11 touchdown passes and one interception over his last three games.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 43: straight drives without an opponent touchdown for Buffalo
top.dek: The Bills defense has kept opponents out of the end zone for 43 consecutive drives and 15 straight quarters. It is the longest single-season streak since the 2019 Patriots, and the last touchdown against Buffalo came in the Week 8 win over Baltimore.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Bears visit Lions on Thanksgiving with the NFC North on the line
top.dek: Chicago plays at Detroit on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, and both teams are 8-2. Watch how the Bears protect Caleb Williams against a Lions front that just lost Aidan Hutchinson for the season.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills win sixth straight, 26-9 over Miami

stories.text: Bills beat Dolphins 26-9 for sixth straight win
stories.summary: Buffalo moved to 9-1 with a 26-9 win over Miami at Highmark Stadium. Josh Allen threw for 304 yards and a 4-yard touchdown to DJ Moore, and the Bills never allowed a Dolphins touchdown. Miami managed just three field goals.

stories.text: Oliver's oblique and a short week for Buffalo
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Ed Oliver went on the injury report with an oblique problem and was listed questionable for Miami on Saturday. The Bills play Kansas City four days later, so his Week 12 status will come into focus with Monday's first practice report. Cornerback Christian Benford (groin) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) were ruled out against Miami, and I could not confirm their status for Thursday.

stories.text: James Cook runs his touchdown streak to nine games
stories.summary: Cook carried 22 times for 89 yards and scored from the 1-yard line, his 10th rushing touchdown of the year. He has now scored on the ground in nine straight games, a single-season NFL record. Allen and Cook are also the first teammates to each reach 10 touchdowns in three separate seasons.

stories.text: 43: straight drives without an opponent touchdown
stories.summary: The Bills defense has held opponents out of the end zone for 43 consecutive drives and 15 straight quarters. That is the longest single-season streak in the NFL since the 2019 Patriots. The last touchdown against Buffalo came in the first quarter of the Week 8 win over Baltimore.

stories.text: Bills host Chiefs on Thanksgiving night
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Kansas City on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch whether the touchdown-free defense stays intact on a four-day turnaround, and how the Oliver and Benford situations resolve.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins fall to 1-9 as offense stalls in Buffalo

stories.text: Dolphins lose fourth straight, 26-9 at Buffalo
stories.summary: Miami fell to 1-9 and netted only 86 passing yards against the Bills. Kyle McCord, making his second NFL start, was intercepted by Damar Hamlin and sacked twice by Greg Rousseau. Daniel Carlson's three field goals were the only points.

stories.text: Dolphins lose three more defensive linemen
stories.summary: Zach Sieler is out for the season, and Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers are headed to injured reserve with season-ending injuries, according to Jeff Hafley's Wednesday update. Center Aaron Brewer was in concussion protocol, and Malik Willis and De'Von Achane were unavailable. This is the pre-game report from Nov. 18, and I could not find a post-game update.

stories.text: Jacob Rodriguez piles up 13 tackles and an interception
stories.summary: The linebacker led Miami with 13 tackles, eight of them solo, and picked off a pass in Buffalo. Safety Zayne Anderson added 11 tackles, an interception and a sack. The defense finished with 72 tackles, six quarterback hits and seven passes defensed in a losing effort.

stories.text: 2 of 14: Miami's third-down conversions in Buffalo
stories.summary: The Dolphins converted 14 percent of their third downs and completed 12 of 33 passes for 86 yards against the Bills. Buffalo has led the NFL in third-down defense since Week 8, allowing a 16.7 percent conversion rate.

stories.text: Dolphins host the Jets in a 1 p.m. rematch
stories.summary: Miami hosts New York on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Hard Rock Stadium. The Jets just ended a five-game skid, so this is a real chance for Miami's second win. Watch whether McCord improves with a second week of starter reps.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye out with fractured fibula at the bye

stories.text: Drake Maye fractures fibula, Patriots reach bye at 5-5
stories.summary: Tests showed a fractured right fibula for Maye, who got hurt on the final play of the first drive in the 35-10 loss to Detroit in Munich. No surgery is needed and there is no ligament damage, but he may not return this season. New England is 5-5 and holds the eighth seed in the AFC.

stories.text: A.J. Brown's hamstring sidelines him for multiple weeks
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown has a hamstring injury expected to cost him several games. It is his third stretch of missed time this year, and he has 11 catches for 128 yards in four games. Coach Mike Vrabel said he does not imagine Maye being available for the Nov. 29 game at the Chargers.

stories.text: Maye was putting up a top-five season before the injury
stories.summary: Maye ranked in the NFL's top five in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18) and yards per attempt (8.4). He also ran for 219 yards and three scores. Tommy DeVito is set to take over, with rookie seventh-rounder Behren Morton next in line.

stories.text: 219: rushing yards from Maye, top five among QBs
stories.summary: Maye's 219 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns both ranked in the NFL's top five among quarterbacks before he went down. The ground game gave New England a second way to score that DeVito is not expected to match.

stories.text: Patriots off this week, then at the Chargers
stories.summary: New England is on its bye in Week 11 and returns Sunday, Nov. 29, at the Chargers at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Expect DeVito under center. Los Angeles is 1-9.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets snap five-game skid with 27-24 win in LA

stories.text: Jets beat Chargers 27-24 to end five-game losing streak
stories.summary: New York scored on its first five possessions at SoFi Stadium and held on for its third win of the year. Los Angeles cut the lead to 27-23 on Justin Herbert's 6-yard touchdown pass with 1:58 left, then could not recover. It was the Jets' first win over the Chargers since 2011.

stories.text: Geno Smith plays through an ankle injury
stories.summary: Smith was limited in practice with a left ankle injury picked up against Buffalo, then started and showed no ill effects. Receiver Omar Cooper Jr. was ruled out, so Sterling Shepard moved up from the practice squad. I found no post-game injury reports for the Jets.

stories.text: Rookie David Bailey hits 9.5 sacks with two more
stories.summary: Bailey recorded two sacks, two tackles for loss and a pass breakup, and his season total is now 9.5 sacks. He also has six forced fumbles this year. The Jets sacked Herbert six times in all.

stories.text: 5 for 5: Jets scored on every early possession
stories.summary: New York scored on each of its first five drives and ate 30 minutes of clock doing it. Smith finished 17 of 21 for 176 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to Shepard. The Jets also converted 9 of 11 third downs.

stories.text: Jets visit Miami for a Sunday 1 p.m. game
stories.summary: New York plays at Miami on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Jets are 3-8 and the Dolphins are 1-9. Watch whether Smith's ankle holds up and whether the early-drive scoring carries over.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens lose a sixth straight in a shootout

stories.text: Ravens drop sixth straight, 35-33 to Panthers
stories.summary: Baltimore led 33-32 on Derrick Henry's 15-yard touchdown run, then watched Ryan Fitzgerald kick a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left to give Carolina the lead. Jacoby Brissett threw an interception with 33 seconds to go to end it. The Ravens fell to 4-7 after a game that included three lost fumbles and two muffed punts.

stories.text: Henry clears concussion protocol; Jackson still out
stories.summary: Derrick Henry left the Carolina game in the fourth quarter after a hard fall following his touchdown, then cleared the concussion protocol the same day. He looks set to resume his lead role at Houston. Lamar Jackson is still recovering from surgery on a broken, dislocated thumb, and the team has put the healing window at 6 to 10 weeks.

stories.text: Mike Green opens the scoring with a safety and two sacks
stories.summary: Mike Green had two sacks against Carolina, including a first-quarter safety that put Baltimore on the board first. T.J. Tampa added an end-zone interception of Bryce Young in the third quarter. The defense still gave up 35 points, but Green gave it a lift early.

stories.text: 162: points the Ravens have allowed in five games
stories.summary: Baltimore has given up 162 points over its last five games, an average of just over 32 per game. The Ravens have also committed at least two turnovers in each of their last four games. The Panthers game added four fumbles, three of them lost.

stories.text: Ravens visit Houston before the bye
stories.summary: Baltimore plays at the Texans (4-6) on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS from NRG Stadium, its last game before the bye. Houston beat Indianapolis 26-3 on Thursday night and has won four of its last six. Watch whether the Ravens can stop turning the ball over.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals open Week 11 on Monday night in D.C.

stories.text: Burrow ties Manning's record in a 38-18 rout of Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 35 of 44 for 406 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions in Cincinnati's 38-18 win over the Steelers on Nov. 15. It was his fifth straight game with at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns, which ties Peyton Manning's 2004 NFL record. The Bengals (7-2) play at Washington on Monday night.

stories.text: Two Bengals out, two doubtful for Washington
stories.summary: Guard Dalton Risner (knees) and linebacker Oren Burks (groin) are out for Monday night. Receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) and cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) are doubtful. Guards Dylan Fairchild and Brian Parker II, linebacker Swayze Bozeman, cornerback Dax Hill (illness) and safety Kyle Dugger (quad) are questionable.

stories.text: Ja'Marr Chase: 11 catches, 231 yards against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards in the win over the Steelers. He has 878 receiving yards and seven touchdowns this season. Pittsburgh played off him in coverage, and he beat it with two deep balls, including a 43-yard catch in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: 21: completions before Pittsburgh's first
stories.summary: Burrow completed 21 passes before the Steelers completed one, which ties the most by one team before its opponent's first since 1978. He finished the first half 26 of 34 for 302 yards and three touchdowns. The Bengals lead the league in passing offense at 298.8 yards per game.

stories.text: Bengals at Commanders, Monday night
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays at Washington tonight, Monday, Nov. 23, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Bengals bring the league's top passing offense into a game against a Commanders pass defense ranked 31st. Cincinnati's third-down defense ranks 30th, which is the matchup to watch on the other side.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns rest on a bye, then get Sunday night

stories.text: Browns use bye week to fix the running game and fast starts
stories.summary: Cleveland (6-4) sits in the last AFC playoff spot and used its Week 11 bye to work on a running game that has improved only slightly, according to the Browns' own assessment. The Browns have been outscored 78-13 in first quarters this season. The Raiders game on Nov. 29 was moved to Sunday Night Football.

stories.text: Browns report no injuries during the bye week
stories.summary: Cleveland did not issue an injury report this week. Ronnie Hickman, who had a concussion, was back on the field. Denzel Ward, Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, Quincy Williams and Tytus Howard were watching from the side, and Schwesinger has played through an ankle injury since the Oct. 11 Jets game.

stories.text: Carson Schwesinger piles up 13 tackles against Houston
stories.summary: Schwesinger made 13 tackles (eight solo) in the 27-24 win over the Texans. It was his sixth double-digit tackle game this season and his third in a row. Houston ran for only 88 yards, the second-fewest Cleveland has allowed this season.

stories.text: 55: straight games without a 300-yard passer allowed
stories.summary: The Browns held C.J. Stroud to 211 yards and 21 in the second half of their 27-24 win over Houston. That stretched their streak to 55 consecutive games without allowing a 300-yard passer, the longest active streak in the NFL. Cleveland also erased a 17-point deficit, its fourth double-digit comeback of the year, a franchise record.

stories.text: Raiders visit Cleveland on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: The Browns host Las Vegas (4-6) on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, a game the league moved from the 1 p.m. window. Cleveland is 4-0 at home to start a season for the first time since 1963. Watch the first quarter, where the Browns have struggled all year.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers drop a second straight, 19-16 in Philly

stories.text: Steelers fall 19-16 to an Eagles team that had lost seven
stories.summary: Pittsburgh lost its second straight game and fell to 6-4 against a Philadelphia team that had dropped seven in a row. DK Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter after two personal fouls involving Cooper DeJean. McCarthy said the team expected to win and that he did not get it done.

stories.text: Herbig out against Eagles; five Steelers questionable
stories.summary: Linebacker Nick Herbig (hip, ribs) was downgraded to out on Saturday after missing the week. Linebacker Patrick Queen (hand) and safety DeShon Elliott (knee) were questionable, as were receivers Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (hand) and guard Gennings Dunker (knee), all three on the return-designated list. Post-game updates were not yet available.

stories.text: Practice-squad call-up Max Hurleman leads Pittsburgh receivers
stories.summary: Hurleman, elevated from the practice squad, caught six of seven targets for 61 yards to lead the Steelers, including the late touchdown that cut the score to 19-16. Rookie Germie Bernard added six catches for 40 yards. Aaron Rodgers hit eight different receivers on 30-of-44 passing for 227 yards.

stories.text: 5: sacks Rodgers took in Philadelphia
stories.summary: The Eagles sacked Aaron Rodgers five times, and Pittsburgh ran for only 73 yards on 20 carries. Chris Boswell kicked field goals of 25, 40 and 52 yards, but the offense settled for three points too often. The Steelers finished with 255 net yards.

stories.text: Steelers host Broncos on Black Friday
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts Denver (8-2) on Friday, Nov. 27 at 3 p.m. ET at Acrisure Stadium, streaming on Prime Video. The Steelers have a short week after two straight losses. Watch whether the offense can move without settling for field goals.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans pound Colts 26-3 on Thursday night

stories.text: Texans smother Colts 26-3 to snap out of a slump
stories.summary: Houston bounced back from its loss at Cleveland with a dominant Thursday night at home, moving to 4-6. The defense blocked a 62-yard field goal try, intercepted Daniel Jones and held Indianapolis to 167 total yards. The Texans trail first-place Jacksonville by three games in the AFC South.

stories.text: Braswell carted off after opening kickoff injury
stories.summary: Defensive end Chris Braswell hurt his right leg on the first play of the game, a 40-yard Colts kickoff return, and left in a cart. The Texans ruled him out at once. He had been elevated from the practice squad and it was his first game this season. No diagnosis or timeline has come out yet.

stories.text: Will Anderson Jr. keeps the NFL sack lead at 11.5
stories.summary: Anderson sacked Daniel Jones in the end zone for a safety against the Colts and added two tackles for loss. His 11.5 sacks lead the league. He played the previous week on a sore ankle in the loss to Cleveland, and Thursday looked like a return to form.

stories.text: 107: David Montgomery's yards in his return from injury
stories.summary: Montgomery carried 26 times for a season-high 107 yards in his first game back from a groin injury that cost him four games. Houston ran the ball steadily enough to keep Indianapolis from controlling the clock.

stories.text: Texans host the Ravens on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Houston plays Baltimore at home on Nov. 29. Watch whether the pass rush stays this active without Braswell, and whether Montgomery keeps carrying the load now that he is healthy again.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts cut Daniel Jones, turn to Richardson

stories.text: Colts waive Daniel Jones one day after 26-3 loss
stories.summary: Indianapolis waived Jones on Friday, and coach Shane Steichen called it best for both sides. Jones re-signed in March on a two-year, $88 million deal. He led the NFL with 13 interceptions and posted career lows in completion rate and yards per attempt. Anthony Richardson Sr. is now the starter.

stories.text: Colts lose McGowan to a hamstring, play without both corners
stories.summary: Running back Seth McGowan strained a hamstring against Houston and did not return. Starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward both sat out the game. Indianapolis has not yet updated their status for Sunday.

stories.text: Anthony Richardson Sr. gets his first start in two years
stories.summary: Steichen named Richardson the starter for the Giants game. The 2023 fourth overall pick has thrown only four passes this season, completing two for 8 yards, and has run three times for 6 yards. He is in the last year of his rookie contract.

stories.text: 167: total yards for the Colts in their worst offensive night
stories.summary: Indianapolis ran for only 38 yards and never reached the end zone against Houston, its first game without a touchdown since November 2024. Kicker Spencer Shrader made a 34-yard field goal but missed from 56 and had a 62-yard try blocked.

stories.text: Colts host the Giants on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Indianapolis plays New York at home on Nov. 29 with Richardson under center. Watch how much the Colts lean on Jonathan Taylor and the run game to keep the new quarterback comfortable.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars stumble 23-18 at the Giants

stories.text: Giants beat Jaguars 23-18 after a 20-6 halftime lead
stories.summary: Jacksonville lost for the first time since Week 6 and fell to 7-3, though it still leads the AFC South by three games. Trevor Lawrence threw two interceptions and the Jaguars turned a replay ruling on a Parker Washington catch into a field goal instead of a touchdown. Coach Liam Coen said his team was outplayed.

stories.text: Left tackle Walker Little leaves with a knee injury
stories.summary: Little, the starting left tackle, left the loss to New York with a knee injury and Wyatt Milum replaced him. Cornerback Jarrian Jones also left early with a chest injury, according to the team's game report. Running back Bhayshul Tuten went into the game hurt and was injured again late. Center Robert Hainsey was out.

stories.text: Parker Washington posts 8 catches, 103 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Washington led Jacksonville's receivers with eight catches for 103 yards. Officials also ruled a fourth-quarter third-and-9 grab at the Giants' 12 incomplete, the replay held, and Jacksonville settled for a field goal. Brian Thomas Jr. later caught an 18-yard score.

stories.text: 1 of 6: Jaguars' touchdown rate in the red zone
stories.summary: Jacksonville threw 12 passes inside the 20 and ran twice for one yard. Lawrence completed four of those 12. The team also took 13 penalties for 107 yards, eight of them before the snap.

stories.text: Jaguars host the Titans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Jacksonville faces 1-9 Tennessee at EverBank Stadium on Nov. 29, a team it beat 40-23 in Nashville a week before the Giants game. Watch the red zone play calling and the status of the left tackle spot.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans fall 51-30 in Dallas, sink to 1-9

stories.text: Cowboys score on first six drives in 51-30 rout of Titans
stories.summary: Dallas scored a touchdown on each of its first six possessions and Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns. Tennessee dropped to 1-9 and clinched its fifth straight losing season, its longest such run since the franchise left Houston.

stories.text: Titans lose Flott, Moore and more in a thin Dallas game
stories.summary: Safety Tony Adams barely played because of illness, cornerback Cor'Dale Flott left with a neck injury and left tackle Dan Moore Jr. left with a knee injury. Safety Terrell Burgess also hurt a knee. Guards Peter Skoronski and Fernando Carmona Jr. did not play.

stories.text: Cam Ward goes 21 of 30 for 248 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Ward hit Carnell Tate on a career-long 59-yard touchdown and added a rushing score. He lost a fumble on a fourth-quarter strip sack and took five sacks behind a banged-up line. Tennessee has scored at least 23 points in five straight games.

stories.text: 3: straight games the Titans allowed 40 or more points
stories.summary: Tennessee gave up 51 to Dallas after allowing 40 to Jacksonville the week before. The Sports Illustrated team site says it is the second time in franchise history and the first since 2004.

stories.text: Titans visit the Jaguars on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Tennessee travels to Jacksonville on Nov. 29. The Titans need answers on the offensive line and in the secondary after a week of injuries, and they get a Jaguars team that wants to bounce back from its own loss.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos run past Raiders for sixth straight win

stories.text: Broncos beat Raiders 38-24 for sixth straight win
stories.summary: Denver improved to 8-2 with a 38-24 win at Empower Field. Jonah Coleman ran 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns, all career highs. Ja'Quan McMillian sealed it with a 35-yard pick-six late in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Harvey stays on IR as Hufanga returns from ankle injury
stories.summary: Running back RJ Harvey is on injured reserve and cannot return before Week 13 against Miami. Safety Talanoa Hufanga came back from an ankle injury and played against Las Vegas. Coleman has carried the load in the backfield while Harvey is out.

stories.text: Jonah Coleman scores three rushing touchdowns in a career day
stories.summary: Coleman carried 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns, and he caught four passes for 18 yards. He has now scored a rushing touchdown in three straight games. His scores covered 1, 4 and 7 yards.

stories.text: 31: Sacks by Denver this season, against 12 allowed
stories.summary: The Broncos sacked Fernando Mendoza five times and hit him 10 times in Sunday's win. That lifts their season total to 31 sacks while their offensive line has given up 12. Alex Singleton led the defense with 11 tackles and a sack.

stories.text: Broncos visit Steelers on Black Friday
stories.summary: Denver plays at Pittsburgh on Friday, Nov. 27, at 3 p.m. ET on Prime Video. It is a short week on the road. Watch whether the ground game keeps rolling without Harvey.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs rout Cardinals, win third straight

stories.text: Chiefs rout Cardinals 34-7 for third straight win
stories.summary: Kansas City led 14-0 before Arizona had gained three yards and never let up. Patrick Mahomes threw three touchdown passes, and the defense held the Cardinals to 205 yards. The Chiefs are 8-2.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker out again; two more Chiefs hurt in win
stories.summary: Running back Kenneth Walker III missed a second straight game with a groin injury, and his status for Thanksgiving night is unclear. Fullback Ben VanSumeren (knee) and tight end Noah Gray (ribs) left Sunday's game early. Travis Kelce played through ankle and calf injuries.

stories.text: Kelce passes Gronkowski with two touchdowns
stories.summary: Travis Kelce caught six passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns. His first score was the 109th touchdown of his career, playoffs included, which moved him past Rob Gronkowski for third-most by a tight end.

stories.text: 7: Sacks for George Karlaftis over four games, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Karlaftis recorded 2.5 sacks against Arizona. That gives him seven in the last four games, the most in the league over that span. Kansas City has held opponents under 14 points six times this season.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Bills on Thanksgiving night
stories.summary: Kansas City plays at Buffalo on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch the running back room, since Walker has missed two straight games and rookie Emmett Johnson has filled in with 143 scrimmage yards against Arizona.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza throws three TDs, Raiders still fall to Denver

stories.text: Raiders fall to Broncos 38-24, lose third straight
stories.summary: Las Vegas dropped to 4-7 despite 370 total yards, 143 rushing yards at nearly six yards a carry and three touchdown passes from rookie Fernando Mendoza. A late pick-six by Ja'Quan McMillian ended any comeback hope.

stories.text: Bowers misses Denver game, aims to return in Week 12
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers sat out with a right ankle injury he suffered on the opening drive against Seattle, plus a quadriceps issue. Coach Klint Kubiak said he made progress and the team targets his return against Cleveland. Backup Michael Mayer left in the fourth quarter with a back injury.

stories.text: Ashton Jeanty piles up 169 yards from scrimmage
stories.summary: Jeanty ran 11 times for 79 yards and caught five passes for 90 yards. He also caught Mendoza's first touchdown pass, a 68-yarder.

stories.text: 267: Passing yards for Mendoza in his second career start
stories.summary: Mendoza completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Denver sacked him five times for 40 yards. Jack Bech caught eight passes for 88 yards and a score.

stories.text: Raiders visit Browns on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at Cleveland on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch Bowers' status and whether Mendoza keeps producing through the air.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Herbert in concussion protocol after loss to Jets

stories.text: Chargers fall to Jets 27-24 and drop to 1-9
stories.summary: Los Angeles lost at home after falling behind by 14. The offense scored a season-high 24 points, including two fourth-quarter touchdowns, but the defense allowed 9 of 11 third-down conversions, including the game-ending third-and-7.

stories.text: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol
stories.summary: The Chargers announced after the game that Herbert is in the NFL concussion protocol. He took six sacks, two on the final possession. Rookie edge rusher Akheem Mesidor left in the first half with an ankle injury, and the team has not given an update.

stories.text: Ladd McConkey returns with two touchdowns
stories.summary: McConkey came back from a back issue that cost him two games and caught five passes for 37 yards and two touchdowns. It was his first multi-touchdown game since late in his rookie season.

stories.text: 158: Rushing yards for the Chargers at 5.3 a carry
stories.summary: Omarion Hampton ran 14 times for 89 yards, including a 36-yard run that was his longest of 2026. The ground game worked, but the defense gave up 165 rushing yards to the Jets, its second-most allowed this season.

stories.text: Chargers host Patriots in Week 12
stories.summary: Los Angeles hosts New England on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:05 p.m. ET (1:05 p.m. PT) on CBS. Herbert's concussion status is the main question heading into the week.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys score 51 and win a shootout

stories.text: Cowboys hang 51 on Titans and get back to 5-6
stories.summary: Dallas scored touchdowns on its first six drives and rolled Tennessee 51-30 at home. The win ended a loss to San Francisco and keeps the Cowboys in the NFC East race at 5-6. They now turn to a short week against Philadelphia.

stories.text: Dak Prescott wraps his left hand but expects to play
stories.summary: Prescott left the Titans game with his left hand wrapped and said he will be fine. No other Cowboys injuries came out of Sunday, so the short week looks clean so far. Watch Prescott's practice reps before Thursday.

stories.text: Dak Prescott throws four TDs without a pick
stories.summary: Prescott went 28 of 33 for 325 yards and four touchdowns, and ran one in. CeeDee Lamb caught 11 passes for 132 yards, and George Pickens added seven for 102. Prescott has 11 touchdown passes and one interception over his last three games.

stories.text: 6 for 6: Cowboys score a TD on every opening drive
stories.summary: Dallas scored touchdowns on its first six possessions against Tennessee. The Cowboys say that has not happened since the stat was first recorded in 1993. It was also their first 50-point game since 2022.

stories.text: Eagles visit AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Dallas hosts Philadelphia on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 4:30 p.m. ET on Fox. The Cowboys finished with 11 penalties for 128 yards against Tennessee, and the secondary gave up a 59-yard touchdown. Those are the fixes to watch on a short week.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants beat Jaguars, hold NFC East lead

stories.text: Giants top Jaguars 23-18 and move to 6-3-1
stories.summary: New York held off Jacksonville at MetLife Stadium and stayed on top of the NFC East. Jameis Winston scored the go-ahead sneak, and the defense forced a turnover on downs and picked off Trevor Lawrence twice. The win ended Jacksonville's three-game streak.

stories.text: Greg Newsome leaves with an ankle injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Greg Newsome II hurt his ankle on the opening drive and did not return. Paulson Adebo stepped in and finished with his first interception of the year. Watch Newsome's practice status ahead of the trip to Indianapolis.

stories.text: Abdul Carter posts two sacks and 12 pressures
stories.summary: Carter recorded a career-high two sacks and four quarterback hits against Jacksonville. It was his first multi-sack game of the season. He kept Lawrence under pressure all afternoon.

stories.text: 8: Dominic Zvada ties the Giants' 50-yard FG record
stories.summary: Zvada hit field goals from 53, 54 and 43 yards against the Jaguars. He now has eight kicks of 50 yards or more this season, which ties the franchise single-season record. Punter Jordan Stout also averaged 60.3 yards on four punts.

stories.text: Giants head to Indianapolis to face the 3-8 Colts
stories.summary: New York plays at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Giants are 6-3-1 and the Colts are 3-8. With the Cowboys at 5-6, the Giants want to protect their lead over the NFC East field.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles end a seven-game losing streak

stories.text: Eagles snap a seven-game skid with 19-16 win over Steelers
stories.summary: Philadelphia beat Pittsburgh at Lincoln Financial Field for its first win since Sept. 20. The Eagles leaned on their defense and kicker Jake Elliott, and Saquon Barkley scored on a 38-yard run. The team is 3-7 with Dallas next on Thanksgiving.

stories.text: Quinyon Mitchell out with a hamstring injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell left the Steelers game with a hamstring injury and did not return. Barkley also hurt his left arm and sat out the rest of the game. Both need to be tracked closely, because the Eagles play Thursday.

stories.text: Jake Elliott kicks the Eagles past Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Elliott made field goals of 41, 53 and 55 yards in a three-point win. He is now 4 for 4 from 50 yards or more this season. Philadelphia needed every one of them.

stories.text: 7: Eagles end a seven-game losing streak
stories.summary: The 19-16 win over Pittsburgh was Philadelphia's first since Sept. 20. The defense held the Steelers to 255 net yards, 73 of them on the ground. Pittsburgh's DK Metcalf was ejected after two personal fouls.

stories.text: Eagles visit Cowboys on Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Philadelphia plays at AT&T Stadium in Arlington on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 4:30 p.m. ET on Fox. The Eagles are 3-7 and Dallas is 5-6. Watch Mitchell and Barkley, who both left Sunday hurt.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders host Bengals on Monday night

stories.text: Commanders host Bengals on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Washington is 3-5-1 and plays Cincinnati tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Commanders beat the Giants 24-21 last Thursday on a late Jayden Daniels touchdown pass. Former Washington tackle Jonathan Allen returns to Northwest Stadium with the Bengals.

stories.text: Four Commanders listed questionable for Bengals
stories.summary: Running backs Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) and Rachaad White (heel), center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and cornerback Amik Robertson (ankle) were listed questionable. Croskey-Merritt, White and Patrick looked likely to play. Daniels (left elbow) practiced fully.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels leads another late comeback
stories.summary: Daniels went 23 of 33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns against the Giants. Stefon Diggs caught the winner from 32 yards out with 57 seconds left, and Rasul Douglas sealed it with an interception. Washington is 5-0-1 in its last six against New York.

stories.text: 207: Daniels' interception-free streak ends
stories.summary: Daniels had thrown 207 straight passes without an interception before the Giants game. He then threw two in the 24-21 win. He still finished with three touchdown passes.

stories.text: Bengals visit Landover tonight on ESPN
stories.summary: Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET at Northwest Stadium. Cincinnati ranks first in the league in passing offense at 298.8 yards per game, and Washington ranks 31st in pass defense. Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase test a defense that gave up 293 passing yards to the Giants.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears win five straight, Simmons wrecks Saints

stories.text: Bears beat Saints 21-13 for a fifth straight win
stories.summary: Chicago improved to 8-2 at Soldier Field behind a defense that piled up six sacks and 10 tackles for loss. The offense gained 311 yards and Caleb Williams threw an interception, so the Bears left talking about what they still need to fix. The Saints cut the lead to one score late, and Luther Burden III recovered the onside kick to end it.

stories.text: Roschon Johnson leaves with ankle injury
stories.summary: Running back Roschon Johnson went down with an ankle injury in the first quarter and did not return. Offensive lineman Theo Benedet also left in the fourth quarter with 7:48 remaining. Neither player has an official update yet, so watch the practice report before Thursday.

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons posts three sacks against New Orleans
stories.summary: The tackle added three tackles for loss and three quarterback hits to his three sacks. He now has five sacks in three games since Chicago got him from Tennessee on Oct. 29 for two first-round picks. Teammates say he has become a voice the locker room follows.

stories.text: 5: Bears wins in a row without ever trailing
stories.summary: Chicago has not trailed in any of its five straight victories. The Bears went 8-2 on Sunday even though the offense managed 311 yards and the running backs gained 69 yards on 21 carries. Williams said the team is not satisfied.

stories.text: Bears visit Lions on Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Chicago plays at Detroit on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, with a stream on Paramount+. Both teams are 8-2 and tied atop the NFC North. Watch how the Bears protect Williams against a Lions front that just lost Aidan Hutchinson.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions win sixth straight, lose Hutchinson

stories.text: Lions pull away from Buccaneers 31-21
stories.summary: Detroit won its sixth straight to reach 8-2. Jared Goff threw for 279 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, and the Lions scored 14 points in the fourth quarter to break it open. Jameson Williams caught four passes for 93 yards and a score.

stories.text: Hutchinson out for the season with right knee injury
stories.summary: Aidan Hutchinson hurt his right knee celebrating a sack of Drake Maye on Nov. 15, and a source told the AP the injury ends his season. He had six sacks in nine games. Cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) were inactive Sunday, and Khalil Dorsey returned after a first-half wrist injury.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs runs for 98 yards against the league's top run defense
stories.summary: Gibbs scored on a 1-yard run and a 4-yard run in the fourth quarter. Tampa Bay entered allowing a league-low 79 rushing yards per game. His touchdowns turned a close game into a 10-point win.

stories.text: 7 of 11: Lions third-down conversions against Tampa Bay
stories.summary: That is a 63.6 percent rate, far above Detroit's season mark of 39.4 percent. The Lions also went 3 for 3 in the red zone. Goff added a season-high 10-yard scramble to convert a third down.

stories.text: Lions host Bears on Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Chicago on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Ford Field. Both teams are 8-2. The Lions play their first Thanksgiving game without Hutchinson, so the pass rush is the thing to watch.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers return from bye hoping Parsons debuts

stories.text: Packers sit last in the NFC North after bye
stories.summary: Green Bay is 6-4 after a 30-10 loss to Minnesota on Nov. 15 in which Jordan Love was sacked eight times and the offense turned the ball over four times. Three division rivals now hold better records. Seven regular-season games remain, starting Wednesday night against the Rams.

stories.text: Seven Packers return to practice, Parsons nears debut
stories.summary: Running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), cornerback Brandon Cisse (ribs) and receivers Bo Melton and Skyy Moore all returned to practice. Micah Parsons is still working back, and coach Matt LaFleur said his practice work will decide whether he plays Wednesday.

stories.text: Micah Parsons set for a season debut
stories.summary: Parsons has not played in nearly a year after a torn ACL and meniscus injury. He opened his 21-day practice window on Nov. 4. NFL insider Ian Rapoport said on Nov. 22 that Parsons is on track to make his season debut against the Rams.

stories.text: 8: Sacks Jordan Love took against Minnesota
stories.summary: Love was sacked eight times and hit 12 times in the 30-10 loss. Green Bay fell behind 17-0, finished with 220 yards, and went 3 of 10 on third down. Minnesota's defense blitzed him for most of the afternoon.

stories.text: Packers visit Rams on Thanksgiving Eve
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix. Both teams are 6-4. Watch whether Parsons plays and whether the offensive line holds up against pressure.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings routed 35-10 by 49ers in Mexico City

stories.text: 49ers blow out Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City
stories.summary: Minnesota fell to 7-3 and dropped to third in the NFC North, holding the No. 6 seed. A Kirk Cousins interception returned for a touchdown made it 28-10 before halftime. The Vikings also lost a fumble on a Justin Jefferson catch that ended any comeback hopes.

stories.text: Isaiah Rodgers inactive with a quad injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers sat out in Mexico City with a quad injury he suffered in practice. No other Vikings injuries were reported from the game. His status for Sunday against Atlanta is not yet known.

stories.text: Kirk Cousins struggles in his second Vikings debut run
stories.summary: Cousins went 26 of 38 for 235 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, a 73.9 rating. Minnesota got him from the Raiders on a Tuesday before the deadline, when he had 20 touchdown passes and 2,340 yards. He led a 9-play, 90-yard drive that tied the game 7-7 before the game got away.

stories.text: 15 of 39: Cousins dropbacks the 49ers pressured
stories.summary: San Francisco pressured Cousins on 15 of his 39 dropbacks, and he averaged 4.0 yards per attempt when the 49ers did not blitz. Minnesota ran 46 plays to San Francisco's 31 through the first 39 minutes and still trailed 28-10.

stories.text: Vikings host Falcons on Sunday
stories.summary: Minnesota plays Atlanta on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET at home. The Vikings need to clean up turnovers and protect Cousins after an offense that went 1 of 3 in the red zone in Mexico City.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons use the bye to self-scout a 3-game skid

stories.text: Stefanski calls the bye a time for hard lessons
stories.summary: Atlanta has lost three straight and five of its last six, and sits last in the NFC South at 3-7. Kevin Stefanski said the team will self-scout during the bye and took responsibility for slow starts. Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees keeps the play calling.

stories.text: Deablo gets time to heal a fractured forearm
stories.summary: Linebacker Divine Deablo has played with a cast on a fractured right forearm and sat out the loss to Kansas City. The bye gives him extra time to recover. Receiver Drake London was cleared after a concussion check in that game.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson stays busy as the offense stalls
stories.summary: Robinson ran 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City, plus four catches for 6 yards. He fell to third in the NFL rushing race after Week 10, behind Buffalo's James Cook at 971 yards. Falling behind 21-3 cut his touches in the second half.

stories.text: 85-30: the margin during Atlanta's three-game skid
stories.summary: The Falcons have been outscored 85-30 over three straight losses. Michael Penix Jr. threw six interceptions and one touchdown in those games after starting the year with nine touchdowns and one interception in his first five starts.

stories.text: Falcons visit the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29
stories.summary: Atlanta was off in Week 11 and plays at Minnesota next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch whether Penix protects the ball after the self-scout. Atlanta opened against Kansas City without a first down on its first four drives.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Young wins another one late as Carolina leads the South

stories.text: Young drives Panthers past Ravens 35-33
stories.summary: Bryce Young marched 55 yards in the final minutes, and Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left. The teams traded the lead seven times. Carolina is 5-5 with two straight wins and a two-game cushion in the NFC South.

stories.text: Mike Jackson returns to the secondary after missing 7 games
stories.summary: Cornerback Mike Jackson was active against Baltimore, his first game since Week 3. Tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller were both questionable with knee injuries heading into the game. Jaycee Horn has been out since Week 3.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard runs for 120 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Hubbard rushed for 120 yards and two touchdowns, including an 18-yard run before halftime. Carolina needed every point in a game with seven lead changes.

stories.text: 14: game-winning drives for Bryce Young
stories.summary: Sunday's march was the 14th game-winning drive of Young's career. He finished 22 of 30 for 254 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Carolina had been 0-5 this season when he threw a pick before Sunday.

stories.text: Panthers visit Tampa Bay on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Carolina plays at Tampa Bay on Monday, Nov. 30 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Buccaneers beat Carolina 43-13 in Week 7, so the Panthers have a score to settle with a division rival.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints drop a third straight in Chicago

stories.text: Turnovers and sacks sink Saints in Chicago, 21-13
stories.summary: New Orleans fell to 3-7 with its third straight loss. The Saints gained 307 yards to Chicago's 311 but failed to score a touchdown on their last eight possessions. Kellen Moore said stalled openers are too common and that the team has to finish drives.

stories.text: Juwan Johnson hurts hamstring, line stays thin
stories.summary: Tight end Juwan Johnson left in the second half with a hamstring injury, and Moore said he is still being evaluated. William Sherman started at center with Cesar Ruiz sliding to guard on a line that has been short on healthy bodies.

stories.text: Chris Olave posts 9 catches for 102 yards
stories.summary: Olave led the Saints through the air with nine catches for 102 yards, and Devaughn Vele added seven for 76. Travis Etienne Jr. ran 14 times for 76 yards, including a 46-yarder that set up New Orleans' lone touchdown.

stories.text: 6: sacks of Tyler Shough, one for a safety
stories.summary: Chicago sacked Shough six times, three by Jeffery Simmons. Montez Sweat's sack in the end zone produced a fourth-quarter safety. Shough finished 25 of 42 for 222 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

stories.text: Saints travel to Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 29
stories.summary: New Orleans plays at the Bengals at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Saints need a faster start. Moore's offense is averaging 0.9 first-quarter points per game through ten games.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs unravel late in Detroit, fall to 3-7

stories.text: Self-inflicted mistakes cost Bucs in 31-21 loss to Lions
stories.summary: Tampa Bay fell to 3-7 after a late rally came up short. Todd Bowles said the Lions did their best things better than the Bucs did theirs, and that his team must win out. Seven games remain, four against NFC South teams.

stories.text: Mayfield plays hurt as two corners leave in Detroit
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield played through a foot injury and finished 20 of 33 for 187 yards and two touchdowns. Corners Jacob Parrish (back) and Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) left the game, and Antoine Winfield Jr. did not play.

stories.text: Rookie Ted Hurst III catches two touchdowns
stories.summary: Hurst caught five passes for 56 yards and both of Mayfield's touchdown passes, a 23-yarder before halftime and a 4-yarder late. They were his second and third scores of the season, after he played a single snap and was benched in Week 9.

stories.text: 80: yards on an Irving touchdown erased by holding
stories.summary: A holding call on right tackle Luke Goedeke early in the third quarter wiped out Bucky Irving's apparent 80-yard touchdown run. Irving still scored from a yard out and gained 100 scrimmage yards. Tampa Bay also lost a fourth-and-1 at the Detroit 10 in the first quarter.

stories.text: Bucs host Panthers on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Tampa Bay hosts Carolina on Monday, Nov. 30 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Bucs beat the Panthers 43-13 in Week 7, but Carolina now leads the division by two games.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Fourth starting QB in four weeks sinks Arizona

stories.text: Cardinals turn to 40-year-old Josh Johnson and fall 34-7 at Kansas City
stories.summary: Arizona dropped to 3-8 and has now started four different quarterbacks in four weeks. Johnson, who signed 12 days earlier and got one practice with the first team, went 18 of 31 for 155 yards and a touchdown. Rookie Carson Beck was set to start until back spasms flared up late in Thursday's practice.

stories.text: Beck's back and a thin QB room lead Arizona's injury list
stories.summary: Beck's back spasms kept him out against the Chiefs, and his status for Washington is unsettled. Gardner Minshew went on injured reserve Nov. 11 with an elbow injury, and receiver Michael Wilson was absent Sunday. Undrafted rookie Joey Aguilar dressed as Johnson's backup.

stories.text: Trey McBride catches 9 on a season-high 14 targets
stories.summary: McBride gave the offense its only steady target with nine catches for 54 yards. The 14 targets were a season high. The Cardinals still scored just seven points.

stories.text: 205: Arizona's total yards against 435 for Kansas City
stories.summary: The Cardinals managed 130 net passing yards, went 5 of 13 on third down and 0 of 2 on fourth down. Kansas City scored on all five first-half possessions. The failed fourth-and-1 at the Arizona 37 turned a 17-7 game into 27-7 by halftime.

stories.text: Commanders visit Glendale on Sunday, Nov. 29
stories.summary: Arizona hosts Washington at State Farm Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch the quarterback decision first: Johnson could start again if Beck's back does not clear. The offense has scored 16 points in its last three games combined.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams rest on four straight wins before Packers

stories.text: Rams ride a four-game win streak out of the bye
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat Arizona 34-6 on Nov. 15 for its fourth straight win and went into the bye at 6-4. They trailed 6-3 early, then scored 31 unanswered points. The Rams sit ninth in the NFC and host Green Bay on Thanksgiving Eve.

stories.text: Nacua needs MCL surgery; Turner and Dedich near returns
stories.summary: Puka Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and had turf toe against Washington, chose surgery Nov. 17 and is out "a couple months," per Sean McVay. Kobie Turner (groin) and Justin Dedich (hand) opened their practice windows off injured reserve. Davante Adams (hamstring) is not ready yet, with a return possible the week after Green Bay.

stories.text: Blake Corum runs for 100 yards on 17 carries
stories.summary: Corum carried 17 times for 100 yards and a 1-yard touchdown against Arizona, his second 100-yard game of the season. He ran behind a line that lost Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon at halftime. Matthew Stafford threw 3 touchdowns to nine different receivers.

stories.text: 31: unanswered points after Arizona led 6-3
stories.summary: The Rams opened slowly in the desert, then scored 31 straight points to win 34-6. Kamren Kinchens and rookie Wesley Bailey each intercepted a pass. Aaron Donald recorded his first sack of the season.

stories.text: Packers visit SoFi on Wednesday night
stories.summary: Los Angeles hosts Green Bay on Thanksgiving Eve, Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 5 p.m. PT (8 p.m. ET) on Netflix. Both teams are 6-4 and chasing NFC playoff spots. Watch how the Rams replace Nacua's targets and whether Turner and Dedich are active.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers rout Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City

stories.text: 49ers beat Minnesota 35-10 and hold the top NFC spot
stories.summary: San Francisco improved to 9-1 with a blowout at Estadio Banorte. Brock Purdy went 21 of 26 for 255 yards and three touchdowns, and the offense scored on three of its first four drives. The win was Kyle Shanahan's 100th, counting the postseason.

stories.text: Right tackle McKivitz breaks and dislocates his left ankle
stories.summary: Colton McKivitz went down in the second quarter with a fractured and dislocated left ankle. Shanahan compared it to the injury that ended Fred Warner's season last October. Mike Evans returned from a two-game absence with an Achilles injury and finished with 109 yards.

stories.text: Mike Evans returns with 6 catches, 109 yards and a touchdown
stories.summary: Evans led the team in catches and yards after missing two games with an Achilles injury. His one-handed 4-yard score made it 21-10 in the second quarter. George Kittle added two touchdowns on three catches for 34 yards.

stories.text: 98: yards on the drive that sealed it for San Francisco
stories.summary: The 49ers led 28-10 at the half, then marched 98 yards for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter. Kirk Cousins threw a pick-six to Ji'Ayir Brown before the half. He had thrown one against San Francisco for the Raiders earlier this season, making him the first player to throw pick-sixes for two teams against the same opponent in one season.

stories.text: Seahawks visit Levi's Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29
stories.summary: San Francisco hosts Seattle on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. The Seahawks come off a bye, and Sam Darnold could return from his quad and rib injuries. Watch who replaces McKivitz at right tackle.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks rest at 6-4, eye Darnold's return

stories.text: Seahawks use the bye to get their quarterback right
stories.summary: Seattle is 6-4 after back-to-back wins over Arizona and Las Vegas. Mike Macdonald says he is "really optimistic" Sam Darnold can start at San Francisco on Nov. 29, and he rejected any talk of a switch to Drew Lock. Seattle sits eighth in the NFC.

stories.text: Darnold works back from a cracked rib and quad injury
stories.summary: Darnold cracked a rib in the Monday night loss to Chicago, then hurt his quad late in that game. He has missed the last two games. Macdonald said Darnold still has recovery hurdles to clear during the bye, and the team hopes for a full week of practice.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the league with 1,207 yards
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba has 79 catches, 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns through 10 games. He is the only NFL receiver over 1,000 yards, with Dallas's CeeDee Lamb next at 976. He accounts for 52 percent of Seattle's receiving yards.

stories.text: 144: Smith-Njigba's receiving yards in one quarter
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba put up 144 yards in the third quarter against the Raiders, a Seahawks single-quarter record. He finished with 8 catches for 171 yards and a 71-yard touchdown. Lock threw for 240 yards and two scores but lost two fumbles in the 21-13 win.

stories.text: Seattle visits the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29
stories.summary: The Seahawks are off in Week 11 and play at San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox at Levi's Stadium. The 49ers beat Seattle 32-29 at Lumen Field in Week 5. A win would cut the division gap and boost Seattle's playoff standing.
